chapter: Road bands: Hucklebuck Williams and Tiny Bradshaw
title: Bradshaw's pay, $35 a night, and learning to be a professional
summary: Bradshaw carries a safe in his car trunk and pays $35 a night against $22 elsewhere.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Getting paid: wages, scale and the pay envelope

blocks.x: Yeah. He had a safe there--back there. And if--if the--if the hall wasn't full by twelve o'clock he'd say pack up.
Pack up. Move to the next town.
And the road manager'd pay 'em off. The safe man, take out a roll [of bills] pay us off.
Yeah. And the--and the--and those road bands, you didn't get but twenty-two dollars a night. Bradshaw paid thirty-five--
You see. I don't care what band you was with, you didn't get no--but twenty--or twenty-two dollars. That was--twenty-two was your highest.
Bradshaw was one of the highest paying bands on the road, man.

Thirty-five dollars a night. Why I made so much money with Bradshaw--boy I had pockets of money, you know, everywhere. You know, and that's how I really learned how to be a professional musician--with him. He fell in love with us--the three of us--cause we were young. And we--and so we stayed clean, you know.
